rationale: Acceptance did not run (no spec), so confidence is low; the other lenses and standards ran. build-installer.ps1 has escape-corrupted path literals that break the build, plus a boot gap, an install race and an update-time runtime wipe; the commit subjects also miss the documented format. 12 findings dismissed or folded as noise or low-severity, 0 deferred.

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires '<type>: <short description>'; all 4 subjects use an 'EPMCDME-15549: ...' prefix and no type
no .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md in the repo and no ref passed; absent standard
no .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md in the repo and no ref passed; absent standard

findings.title: Escape-corrupted path literals break build
findings.problem: Path literals lost their backslash escapes: $PackJson is "assets\windowsuntime-pack.json" (line 39, should be assets\windows\runtime-pack.json), "binuntime-key" (line 168 and the bundle-asset list, should be bin\runtime-key), the node\node.exe 'bundled again' check is split across lines, and the throwaway unpack path is "CodeMieuntime\<key>" (should be CodeMie\runtime\<key>). Test-Path $PackJson is always false and Get-Content $PackJson (line 163) fails.
findings.impact: Step 5 of the Windows build always aborts or checks nonexistent paths. The Node-bundled-again guard can never fire and the shim smoke test unpacks where the shim never looks. No test covers this script.
findings.recommendation: Restore the paths: Join-Path $Root "assets\windows\runtime-pack.json", Join-Path $ReleaseDir "bin\runtime-key", Join-Path $ReleaseDir "node\node.exe", Join-Path $TestLocal "CodeMie\runtime\$($pack.key)". Prefer single-quoted strings or escaped separators.

findings.title: Uninstall hook wipes runtime on every update
findings.problem: RMDir /r "$LOCALAPPDATA\CodeMie\runtime" runs unconditionally in the uninstall macro, with no update-mode guard.
findings.impact: If the old uninstaller runs during an in-place update, each update deletes the roughly 200 MB runtime and forces a re-download. Reachability of the update path was unconfirmed. Under an elevated context it may also resolve to a different user's folder.
findings.recommendation: Skip the RMDir when the uninstall is part of an update (check $UpdateMode), and confirm $LOCALAPPDATA resolves to the installing user's profile.

findings.title: No guard against concurrent runtime installs
findings.problem: ensure_runtime and remove_stale use shared .staging-<key> and .download-<key> paths with no lock, and remove_stale deletes every other entry under the runtime dir. The app has no single-instance plugin, so two instances or a double call can run concurrently.
findings.impact: One call can delete the other's archive or staging mid-write, giving a spurious download failure or a corrupt unpack. An older app version side by side can delete a newer runtime.
findings.recommendation: Serialize with a process-wide async mutex, add the single-instance plugin, and make remove_stale skip entries it does not own.

findings.title: runtime_ready rejection aborts boot silently
findings.problem: ensureRuntime() awaits invoke('runtime_ready') outside any try/catch, and boot() awaits it first. runtime_ready returns Err when LOCALAPPDATA is unset or the baked pack JSON is bad.
findings.impact: boot() rejects, so the app shows no overlay, no Try again and no message. Reachability of the Err path was unconfirmed. The unlisten() leak in the retry loop is a related smaller issue.
findings.recommendation: Catch the rejection and show the runtime overlay with the error and a Try again button, and call unlisten() in a finally block.

findings.title: Commit subjects do not follow documented format
findings.problem: Commits 10120a6, 986dc6f, 336aa31 and fe2af2f use an 'EPMCDME-15549: ...' subject where git-workflow.md requires '<type>: <short description>' with type in feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor.
findings.impact: The commit subjects do not match the format the git workflow guide requires.
findings.recommendation: Reword the subjects to the documented form, for example 'feat: download Node and the CLI on first launch (Windows runtime module)'.
